learningObjective: Compute the approximate weight-loading bandwidth saving of W4A16 vs FP16 for LLM decode.

canonicalClaims.claim: For batch-1 LLM decode (bandwidth-bound on weight loads), W4A16 with group_size=128 reduces weight-load traffic by roughly 4× compared to FP16 (INT4 = 0.5 B/param + FP16 scales at 1/32 overhead ≈ ~0.55 B/param effective).
conditions: Decode is bandwidth-bound (small batch, single request).
The W4A16 kernel achieves close to peak effective bandwidth.
nonImplications: Does not imply the observed wall-clock speedup is exactly 4× — dequant, scale broadcast, and kernel overhead reduce it to 2.5-3× in practice.
Does not imply the same argument holds for prefill / large-batch cases, which are compute-bound.

misconceptions.claim: INT4 weights are stored in FP16-sized buffers, so memory traffic is unchanged.
misconceptions.whyWrong: INT4 weights are packed (two per byte); memory footprint and traffic are ~1/4 of FP16.

misconceptions.claim: Per-group scales at group_size 128 double the metadata size, offsetting the bandwidth savings.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Scales at group_size 128 add one FP16 per 128 INT4 weights = 2 bytes / 64 bytes ≈ 3% overhead, not 100%.

misconceptions.claim: W4A16 delivers 8× decode speedup vs FP16 because INT4 saves 4× bytes and per-channel scaling adds another 2×.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-channel scaling saves no additional bandwidth; the speedup is bounded by 4× (memory-traffic ratio) minus dequant overhead.

misconceptions.claim: W4A16 speedup applies equally to prefill and decode.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Prefill is compute-bound (long sequence, large activation batch), so weight bandwidth is not the bottleneck; W4A16's gain shrinks or vanishes there.

implementationFacts: Marlin and ExLlama INT4 kernels dequant-in-register and use FP16 Tensor Cores.
Group size 128 is standard for AWQ / GPTQ; other options include 32, 64.
performanceScenarios: LLaMA-7B decode on A100 batch=1: FP16 ~35 tokens/s, W4A16 ~90 tokens/s (~2.5× effective speedup).
LLaMA-7B prefill 2k tokens on A100: W4A16 gain shrinks to <1.3× because compute dominates.
